KeyPassages: Exodus 15:20; 1 Samuel 18:6; Judges 11:34; Song of Solomon 6:13
BiblicalUsage: A dance is the movement of joy before God, and the Bible uses it at the great moments of deliverance: Miriam takes a timbrel and leads the women in dances after the sea closes over Pharaoh, the women come out with dances to meet Saul after David kills Goliath, and Jephthah's daughter comes out with timbrels and dances to greet her father. The Song pictures the dance of the two camps, the company of two armies.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe dancing is the body's way of saying what words cannot: Miriam danced because the sea had closed, the women danced because Goliath had fallen, and the joy was too big to stand still for. I hold that the dance of the two camps is the church itself — two armies, one joy, moving together before God.
